report_name: Phishing Breach at Defense Firm IEH Corp Exposes M365 Data

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Phishing Actor
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actor responsible for the spearphishing campaign against IEH Corporation, which involved credential harvesting and creating malicious mailbox rules to access sensitive data.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor sent an email containing a hyperlink disguised as a Microsoft document-sharing link to a targeted employee. The link led to a fraudulent login page to harvest credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attacker gained full access to an employee's Microsoft 365 account after the employee entered their credentials on a fraudulent login page.

attack_patterns.name: Email Forwarding Rule
attack_patterns.description: After gaining access to the employee's mailbox, the attacker set up malicious mailbox rules to maintain access and potentially forward sensitive emails.

identities.name: IEH Corporation
identities.description: A U.S. manufacturer of high-reliability connectors for the defense and aerospace industries that was the victim of a targeted phishing attack, leading to the compromise of an employee's Microsoft 365 account.

infrastructure.name: Fraudulent M365 Login Page
infrastructure.description: A look-alike Microsoft 365 login page used for credential harvesting after a user clicked a spearphishing link.

indicators.name: Suspicious M365 Inbox Rule Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious M365 Inbox Rule Creation
id: 2b8c9a1f-7d3e-4b0c-8a1d-9f6e5b4c3d2a
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a new inbox rule in Microsoft 365. This is often used by attackers for persistence or to forward sensitive emails after an account compromise.
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/196890/cyber-crime/u-s-defense-manufacturer-ieh-hit-by-phishing-attack-exposing-potentially-export-controlled-data.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-10
tags:
  - attack.t1114.003
  - attack.persistence
level: medium
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.exchange
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'New-InboxRule'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of new inbox rules in Microsoft 365, a technique used by the attacker in the IEH Corp breach to maintain persistence.

indicators.name: Suspicious M365 Mailbox Permission Added
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious M365 Mailbox Permission Added
id: 8e1d2c3b-4a5f-4b6c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects when a user adds permissions to another user's mailbox. This could be an attacker granting themselves access to other mailboxes for lateral movement or data collection.
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/196890/cyber-crime/u-s-defense-manufacturer-ieh-hit-by-phishing-attack-exposing-potentially-export-controlled-data.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-10
tags:
  - attack.t1098
  - attack.lateral_movement
level: medium
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.exchange
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'Add-MailboxPermission'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of 'Add-MailboxPermission', a potential sign of an attacker expanding access within a compromised M365 environment, as suggested in the hunting hints for the IEH Corp breach.
